summary: No Blocker. The revision fixes F1 to F11. Probes of the specified rule match every named fixture and the real Math lines. One new Major (F12): the four-value processed tuple of FR-3 cannot mark a deferred parent, which FR-2 needs. Five new Nits (F13 to F17).
nonblocking_findings: F12 [Major] spec.md FR-3 and FR-2: FR-3 fixes each `processed` entry at four values `(indent, status, covered, ignored)`, with `ignored=False` when a line is not ignored. A `deferred` line then has the same four values as an ordinary `[x]` line. The checker stores it as `(indent, status, True)`, or `(indent, status, False)` for a closeout line without a SHA. FR-1(a) ignores a box under any `[x]` line, and FR-2 forbids it under a `deferred` parent. Probe: `- [x] T (deferred)` plus `  - [ ] s` gives one `plan task is not complete` line today and none by the four values. Rationale: a Green that follows FR-3 fails the deferred `[x]` fixture of Task 1.1, so the implementer must add a fifth fact or recode `status`. A recode of `status` changes today's result for `- [x] T (deferred)` plus `  - [x] s` (empty feedback). The revision removed the round 1 sentences that kept `deferred` handling and the SHA rule of nested `[x]` boxes, and no fixture checks them. State the behavior and drop the tuple layout, or add a `deferred` value, and keep `deferred` handling and `[x]` coverage outside an ignored chain as today.

F13 [Nit] spec.md FR-1: The sentence 'A SHA-less `[x]` parent still reports its own `completed plan task lacks commit SHA` line; its nested boxes add no second line' says 'boxes', not 'open boxes'. A nested `[x]` box under a SHA-less `[x]` parent still gets its own SHA line. Probe: `- [x] T`, `  - [x] a`, `  - [x] b`, `    - [ ] c`, `  - [ ] d` gives three SHA lines (T, a, b) and no other line. Rationale: the wording conflicts with FR-3 and with case 2 of `test_subbox_sha.py`, which stays and expects two lines. Write 'nested open boxes'.

F14 [Nit] spec.md Acceptance Criteria and plan.md Task 1.1: The case 'a `[x]` box without a SHA under an ignored `[ ]` box ... the SHA message with an uncovered ancestor' does not give the exact list. The rule gives two lines: the `completed plan task lacks commit SHA` line of the uncovered `[x]` ancestor and the same message for the box. Probe: `- [x] T`, `  - [ ] s`, `    - [x] ss` gives [T, ss]. Rationale: Task 1.1 says each case names an exact list, and a Red that expects one line fails after Green. State the two-line list.

F15 [Nit] plan.md Task 1.1: The `closeout_candidates` case names no fixture tracks and no expected list. Class 2 of `test_subbox_sha.py` builds `expected` from `plan_closeout_feedback`, which is true by construction because `closeout_candidates` calls it. Only the fixed list `["passes"]` checks the rule. Rationale: without a fixed list and a track with a SHA'd `[x]` parent and a nested `[ ]` box, the case passes before Green. Name the tracks and the expected list.

F16 [Nit] spec.md FR-5 and plan.md Task 1.2: The plan updates 'the README.md Status sentence', but README.md holds two `As of` Status sentences: line 33 (2026-11-18, Sub-box SHA rule) and line 34 (2026-11-19, Measure board). Neither says that unticked boxes fail, and line 33 stays true after the change. The plan names no new text. Rationale: the implementer must pick the sentence and the text. The archive commits of earlier tracks rewrite this sentence (bf96031, 4b3d82e), so closeout changes it again. Name the sentence and its text, or move the README edit to closeout.

F17 [Nit] spec.md FR-1 and FR-2: A `[x]` line nested under an open top-level task also grants the ignore by FR-1(a). FR-2 says that a box under a non-ignored open parent fails, and that 'this holds under a top-level `[ ]` or `[~]`'. Probe: `- [ ] T`, `  - [x] a <sha>`, `    - [ ] c` gives only the line of T, so `c` is ignored. Rationale: no fixture checks this, and a reader of the FR-2 sentence can expect `c` to fail. The verdict does not change, because T still fails. Add one fixture or one sentence.

paraphrase.proposes: The track changes plan_closeout_feedback so an indented [ ] or [~] box gives no `plan task is not complete` line. The box is ignored when its nearest shallower parent is an [x] line, covered or not, or an ignored nested open box. Top-level open tasks, boxes under non-ignored open parents, and boxes under deferred parents keep today's feedback. An ignored box is stored with covered False and ignored True, and a [x] box under it takes coverage from its own SHA or the nearest covered [x] ancestor. A new Red test, a rewrite of case 3 of test_subbox_sha.py, and README and CHANGELOG edits go in; track_incomplete, phase_counts, and the jr-green branch stay unchanged.
paraphrase.current_system: plan_closeout_feedback reads each checkbox line and keeps (indent, status, covered) for each line. It appends `plan task is not complete` for each non-[x] line at any depth, before the parent-cover rule runs, except for deferred lines. A nested [x] line is covered by its own SHA or by a covered [x] line that is its nearest parent. track_incomplete and phase_counts read only column-0 lines, so they already ignore nested boxes. Only closeout_candidates and closeout_feedback call plan_closeout_feedback, and the Math plan fails closeout today with 302 feedback lines.
